phase: Pre-step: fast-forward feature/system-details onto origin/master 847ab19 (branch is a strict ancestor; naming workstream already deployed). Increment 1 = AC7 (build-time ingest: exoplanet archive + dim hosts + enlarged real-name blocklist); Increment 2 = AC5 (data-driven authoring path, Alpha Centauri proof — flips the flagged match-radius test per a1d2d4c successor flag 1); Increment 3 = AC3+AC4 (bulk contents overlay + Elite-style procgen fill); Increment 4 = AC2 (player search surface: real + settled/notable + structures — NavComputer UI seam is lane-D-adjacent, route through coordinator); Increment 5 = AC1+AC6 (neighborhood verify + structures audit); AC8 = continuous guardrail per increment; AC9 = Max's batched UAT at the end.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: In the neighborhood of Sol or another famous star, the Nav screen shows the stars Max would expect to see: real neighbors with real names at true positions, including newly ingested dim hosts (e.g. Proxima Centauri, TRAPPIST-1) that are not naked-eye but are nav-instrument-visible.

verifyVia.input: Enter Sol, open the nav computer; repeat from Sirius.
verifyVia.observable: From Sol the nav view/list contains the expected named neighbors (Rigil Kentaurus, Toliman, Proxima Centauri, Barnard's Star, Sirius, Procyon, ...) with distances matching real values within tolerance; newly added dim hosts appear despite being below naked-eye magnitude; no expected famous neighbor is missing or misplaced.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A player-facing search in the nav computer finds a system the player knows about — real star systems (proper name or designation), named settled/notable catalog systems (the ac5 settled-catalog UI ask folds in here), and deep-sky structures — and selecting a result targets it for travel.

verifyVia.input: Open the nav computer search; query 'TRAPPIST-1', 'Sirius', 'M42', and one settled-catalog name from the gazetteer; select each result and travel/warp.
verifyVia.observable: Each query resolves to the right object; selection targets it; warp arrival lands on a system whose name matches the query (structures: nav/travel points at the structure's true position). Search is reachable in normal play without the debug panel.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Systems Max knows about match the characteristics already observed (type of star, known planets, etc.): arriving at a known real system spawns its real structure from the ingested data, not procgen inventions in their place.

verifyVia.input: Warp to Sirius and to TRAPPIST-1 (any targeting path).
verifyVia.observable: Sirius: A-class primary plus its white-dwarf companion present as a binary. TRAPPIST-1: M-dwarf with its seven known planets carrying their real designations (b–h) and archive-derived parameters. Star class matches the sky/catalog on every arrival path.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: When real data runs out, the system fills the rest with procgen (Elite as the guide): known planets appear per the ingested data, procgen deterministically completes the remainder, and real systems with no known planets keep real star parameters with full procgen contents.

verifyVia.input: Headless: generate contents twice for (a) a real system with partial known planets, (b) a real star with zero known planets, through the real arrival pipeline (StarSystemGenerator + overlay merge).
verifyVia.observable: (a) all known planets present with archive-derived parameters, remainder procgen-filled, both runs byte-identical (revisit-stable); (b) real star parameters (type, multiplicity) preserved, planets fully procgen, byte-identical across runs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The ability to author systems and place them over procgen ones exists as a data-driven capability: a KnownSystems registry entry defined as structured data (not a hand-written generate() function) produces full system contents — proven by registering Alpha Centauri (triple star with Proxima's known planets).

verifyVia.input: Register Alpha Centauri as a data-defined entry; arrive via all three paths (nav-warp, sky-click warp, teleport); run the KnownSystems test suites.
verifyVia.observable: All three arrival paths spawn the authored triple system; findAt(RIGIL_POS) resolves to Alpha Centauri (the a1d2d4c successor-flag test flips from 'does NOT match Sol'); alias/belt/sweep tests stay green with the new entry; Proxima's known planets present per the ingested archive.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Famous structures (nebulas and so on) match observation: the shipped deep-sky objects (37 KnownObjectProfiles) and real globular clusters (152, Harris) sit at observed positions and sizes, with discrepancies fixed or explicitly documented.

verifyVia.input: Run a committed headless audit comparing profile/catalog positions and radii against reference catalog values.
verifyVia.observable: Audit report committed to this workstream dir; the famous set (M42, Horsehead/IC434, M78, 47 Tuc, ...) within documented tolerance; each out-of-tolerance entry either corrected or carries a written rationale.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Build-time ingestion delivers the data everything else consumes: re-runnable scripts ingest a public confirmed-exoplanet archive (candidate: NASA Exoplanet Archive — source, license, field coverage, and counts verified in this increment) plus dim famous hosts as new real catalog stars at true positions, with build-time verification.

verifyVia.input: Run the ingestion scripts twice; run the existing naming/catalog test suites against the enlarged data.
verifyVia.observable: Two runs byte-identical; ingested counts reported (systems, planets, new host stars); no duplicate star identities; the enlarged real-proper-name set feeds the procgen blocklist and the named-systems build-time checks with zero collisions (no settled/notable name matches a new real name); the full-catalog sweep test stays green (new hosts near known-system entries resolve via alias membership, not swallow).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The universe that already works stays working: Sol still resolves as Sol with handcrafted contents (always-test-Sol), the full test suite stays green, and purely procedural systems — those touched by no real data — generate byte-identical contents before vs after this workstream (seed-stream isolation holds).

verifyVia.input: Per increment: window._lab.enterSol() + window.__wd.runIntegrationSuite(); full vitest run from the repo dir; a pinned snapshot test over sample procgen-only seeds/positions captured before Increment 1.
verifyVia.observable: Scene suite 19/19 in Sol; vitest fully green (baseline 1123 grows, never shrinks); procgen-only snapshot byte-identical across the workstream.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Max's holistic acceptance: the universe he knows is actually there and findable as a cohesive whole — the nav neighborhood looks right from home, searching finds what he expects, arriving matches what astronomy says, structures included.

verifyVia.input: Max explores freely: nav from Sol, searches systems and structures he knows, warps to Sirius / Alpha Centauri / TRAPPIST-1, checks the fill against his Elite intuition.
verifyVia.observable: Max's pass/fail-with-findings judgment, recorded in this workstream dir. The workflow never marks this AC — deferred-to-max.
